En muchos postes y casetas hay un cajón: On many poles and in many huts there is a grey box that hums. The medium-voltage line cables enter at the top, at about **20,000 V**, and those going to the houses leave at the bottom, at **400 V** between phases (230 V at each socket).\n\nIt has no moving parts, and yet it changes the voltage by a factor of 50 and lets almost all the energy through. Inside there are only two coils of wire and a block of iron. Let us see how it works.

es la relación de vueltas del ejemplo: 5: is the turns ratio of the example: 50 turns of the primary for each one of the secondary.
Un transformador es un anillo de hierro: A transformer is an iron ring with two coils that do not touch. The **primary**, which receives the 20 kV, has many turns ($N_1$ = ${miles(N1)}) of thin wire. The **secondary**, which gives the 400 V, has few ($N_2$ = ${N2}) of thick wire.\n\nThe iron acts as a guide: almost all the magnetic field created by one coil stays inside the core and passes through the other. There is no cable between the two: only the field. (Not all the turns are shown in the drawing.)
es la fem que Faraday da a cada vuelta c: is the emf that Faraday gives each turn at 50 Hz: the same for the primary and the secondary.
La corriente alterna del primario crea e:
The alternating current in the primary creates in the core a flux $Φ$ that rises, falls and reverses 50 times per second. The same flux passes through each turn of any coil, and Faraday's law gives the emf of each:

$ε = −N {dΦ}/{dt}$, so that $ {V_2}/{V_1} = {N_2}/{N_1} $

With 20 kV rms and 2500 turns we get ${n(datos.voltiosPorVuelta, 0)} V per turn; with 50 turns, $V_2$ = **${V2} V**. The maximum flux is $Φ = V_2 √2 / (ω N_2)$ = ${n(PHI * 1000, 1)} mWb, and in a core of 0.04 m², $B$ = ${n(BMAX, 2)} T. Change the number of turns of the secondary.

A transformer does not create energy: almost all the power that goes in comes out. If the pole delivers ${miles(S / 1000)} kVA, $P = V I$ is the same on both sides:

$V_1 I_1 = V_2 I_2$, so that $I_1 = S/V_1$ = **${n(I1, 0)} A** and $I_2 = S/V_2$ = **${miles(I2)} A**

That is why the secondary is made of thick wire (250 A) and the primary of thin wire (5 A). And that is why electricity is transmitted at high voltage: with a small current little is lost in the cables, $P = I^2 R$. The transformer is what allows raising it at the exit of the power station and lowering it on your street.
Por qué solo funciona con alterna: Why it only works with alternating current
con corriente continua: el flujo es cons: with direct current: the flux is constant, its derivative is zero and nothing is induced.
Si conectas el primario a una pila, o a: If you connect the primary to a battery, or to direct current, something curious happens: when connected, the flux grows for an instant and a brief emf appears; after that the flux is constant and **$ε = −N dΦ/dt = 0$**. There is no voltage in the secondary.\n\nIn the primary, the impedance of the coil ($ω L$) is what limits the current when it is alternating; with direct current only the resistance of the wire remains, and the primary burns out. With alternating current, the flux changes continuously and the emf is always there. That is why the grid is alternating current: it won (war of the currents) because the voltage can be raised and lowered with transformers.
es el tono del zumbido: el doble de la r: is the pitch of the hum: twice that of the mains, because the deformation of the iron depends on B², not on its direction.
El hierro no es perfecto. Se deforma un: Iron is not perfect. It deforms slightly when magnetised (magnetostriction) and does so equally with positive and negative B: **twice per cycle**, at 100 Hz. That is the hum you hear.\n\nIn addition, the changing flux creates eddy currents in the core itself, which heat it. That is why it is made of thin sheets of silicon steel, insulated from each other: they cut the swirls and reduce the heat. Even so, a 100 kVA transformer loses around 1 %, about ${n(datos.perdidas / 1000, 1)} kW, which is carried away with oil and fins. That is an efficiency of ${n(REND * 100, 0)} %.
